mainTopic: The משנה listing the basic rules for paying damages, and the גמרא's phrase-by-phrase explanation: שׁוּם כֶּסֶף, שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף (land, and collecting from יתומים), בפני בית דין, and על פי עדים.
overview: The amud opens with a short line that closes the previous discussion: three general rules that apply in four places. Then a new משנה lists the basic framework for paying damages. Damages are appraised in money and paid with things worth money. The case must come before a בית דין, based on valid עדים. Women are included in the laws of damages, and both the ניזק and the מזיק are involved in the payment. The גמרא explains these phrases one by one. רב יהודה says the appraisal must be in money, which matches the ברייתא of the cow and the cloak that damaged each other. A ברייתא reads שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף as land. After two failed explanations by רבה בר עולא, רב אשי explains why the phrase points to land. A contradiction with another ברייתא, which allows payment even with bran, is resolved by saying the land-only rule is about collecting from יתומים. ״בפני בית דין״ is explained as excluding a court of הדיוטות. ״על פי עדים״ is first read as excluding someone who admitted to a קנס. When that is challenged, the גמרא begins to answer that the phrase sets up the next clause, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing summary: three principles in four places
steps.stepSummary: A short summary line that closes the previous discussion. There are three general principles, and they appear in four places.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are three general principles, spread across four places.
steps.whatsHappening: This line wraps up the discussion that came just before it. It is a summing-up line, not a new argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line counts the principles the earlier discussion talked about: there are really three. They are listed as four only because they apply in four different places. After this, the text moves on to a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: general principles or rules
places (here, the places where the rules apply)

phrases.english: Three general principles
in four places.
phrases.notes: The ה in square brackets is the corrected wording, so read it as בְּאַרְבָּעָה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The earlier material comes down to three principles that apply in four places.

steps.title: The משנה: the basic rules of paying damages
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the framework for damages. Damages are appraised in money and paid with things worth money. The case is decided by a בית דין through valid עדים. Women are included. Both sides are involved in the payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Damages are appraised in money and paid with things worth money. This is done before a court, based on witnesses who are free men and members of the covenant. Women are included in the laws of damage. Both the injured party and the one who caused the damage are involved in the payment.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives a short list of rules about how damages get paid. Each phrase is very brief, and the גמרא will explain them one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses very short phrases that need explaining. It covers how the damage is measured (in money), what is paid (things worth money), and who judges (a בית דין). It also says who may testify (בני חורין and בני ברית), that women are included, and that both sides share in the payment.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה
appraisal in money
something worth money (used to pay)
free men (not slaves)
members of the covenant (Jews)
the injured party / the one who caused the damage

steps.confusionAlert: שׁוּם כֶּסֶף and שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף sound almost the same but mean different things. The first is about how the damage is measured. The second is about what may be used to pay.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets up the whole procedure for collecting damages. The גמרא will now go through it phrase by phrase.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Appraisal in money; worth money.

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין, וְעַל פִּי עֵדִים –
phrases.english: Before a court, and based on witnesses
who are free men, members of the covenant.
And women are included in the laws of damage.
And the injured party and the one who caused the damage are involved in the payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the closing line of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damages are appraised in money and paid with things worth money. The case goes before a בית דין with valid עדים. Women are included, and both the ניזק and the מזיק are involved in the payment.

steps.title: What does 'appraisal in money' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by its first phrase, שׁוּם כֶּסֶף.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is meant by 'appraisal in money'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the משנה with its first phrase. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase שׁוּם כֶּסֶף is only two words, so it is not clear what it teaches. The גמרא asks for its meaning before explaining it.

keyTerms.meaning: what is (the meaning of)
appraisal or assessment of value

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is 'appraisal in money'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the first phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase שׁוּם כֶּסֶף in the משנה.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the appraisal must be in money
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the appraisal of the damage must be done only in terms of money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: this appraisal should be done only in money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question. שׁוּם כֶּסֶף means the damage is measured by its value in money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לֹא יְהֵא אֶלָּא' mean 'only'. They tell us the appraisal must be stated as a money amount and in no other terms. This explains the first half of the משנה's opening phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: it should be only

steps.whatToRemember: שׁוּם כֶּסֶף: damage is always appraised in terms of money.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּם זֶה לֹא יְהֵא אֶלָּא בְּכֶסֶף.
phrases.english: This appraisal should be only in money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה שׁוּם זֶה לֹא יְהֵא אֶלָּא בְּכֶסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about שׁוּם כֶּסֶף.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The appraisal of the damage must be made only in terms of money.

steps.title: The cow and the cloak: appraise in money, don't call it even
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה, as רב יהודה explained it, teaches the same law as a ברייתא. When a cow and a cloak damage each other, we do not just call it even. Each damage is appraised in money.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn here what the Sages taught: a cow damaged a cloak, and the cloak damaged the cow. We don't say, 'the cow goes for the cloak and the cloak for the cow.' Instead, we appraise it in money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב יהודה's reading of שׁוּם כֶּסֶף (appraise only in money) is the same law found in a known ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is two damages going in both directions. You might think the two damages simply cancel each other out. The ברייתא says no: each damage is measured in money first, and only then do we see who owes whom. That is exactly the 'appraise only in money' rule from step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Cloak, garment
Let the cow cancel out the cloak (call it even)
Appraise by monetary value

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא means the owners pay nothing. It means we don't assume the damages are equal. We measure each one in money, and whoever caused more damage pays the difference.

phrases.english: We have learned here that which the Sages taught:
A cow that damaged a cloak,
and the cloak damaged the cow,
we do not say:
Let the cow go out against the cloak
phrases.notes: Literally 'go out with.' He means the cow's damage is simply swapped for the cloak's damage, as if they cancel out.

phrases.english: and the cloak against the cow,
rather, we appraise it in money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב יהודה's explanation in step 4 matches an existing ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's reading of שׁוּם כֶּסֶף as appraisal only in money
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the cow and the cloak that damaged each other
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that in two-way damage cases בית דין does not shortcut by calling it even. It measures each loss in money.

steps.title: Moving to the next phrase: worth money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה, שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף, so it can explain it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Worth money.' What does it mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase in the משנה. This is a setup line that gets us ready for the explanation coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not written out, but it is understood: what does the משנה mean by payment with 'something worth money'? The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Something worth money (an item, not cash)

phrases.english: 'Worth money':

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes with שׁוּם כֶּסֶף and moves to the next phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the משנה means by שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף

steps.title: Worth money means land, unless the victim already grabbed movable items
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף teaches that בית דין only collects damages from land. But if the ניזק already seized movable items, בית דין collects for him from those.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages taught: 'Worth money' teaches that בית דין only gets involved with property that carries a guarantee, meaning land. But if the injured person got there first and grabbed movable items, בית דין collects for him from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. 'Worth money' refers to land, and בית דין collects damages from land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נכסים שיש להן אחריות are assets that serve as a guarantee for debts, meaning land. The ברייתא says בית דין only sets out to collect from those. There is one exception: if the ניזק already took hold of movable items (מטלטלין), בית דין lets him collect from what he holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Get involved with, attend to
Property that serves as a guarantee, meaning land
The injured party
Seized, grabbed
Movable property

steps.confusionAlert: שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף sounds like it should mean 'anything of value.' Here the ברייתא reads it as land specifically, and movable items are only an exception.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught: 'Worth money':
this teaches that the court does not attend
except to property that serves as a guarantee.
phrases.notes: This means land, the kind of property a debt can always be collected from.

phrases.english: But if the injured party went ahead
and seized movable property,
the court collects for him from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף means land. בית דין collects damages from land, except from movable items the ניזק already seized.
steps.whatToRemember: שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף = land (נכסים שיש להן אחריות). Movable items only if the ניזק already grabbed them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the normal source for paying damages, land, and leaves room for the ניזק who already holds movable items.

steps.title: How do the words 'worth money' point to land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again and asks how the phrase שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף shows that it means land.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Worth money' teaches that the court only attends to property that serves as a guarantee. Where is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the ברייתא's words so it can look at them closely. It asks how 'worth money' means land, and this sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a ruling but did not show how it fits the words. Nothing in 'worth money' plainly says 'land.' So the גמרא asks for the source in the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Where is this implied? How do we hear it in the words?

phrases.english: The Master said: 'Worth money':
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is the author of the ברייתא we just read.

phrases.english: this teaches that the court does not attend
except to property that serves as a guarantee.
Where is this implied?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: ״שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף״ – מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין נִזְקָקִין אֶלָּא לִנְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן אַחְרָיוּת. מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the ברייתא from step 7 in order to ask how its ruling comes from the words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the phrase שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף shows that it means land

steps.title: First explanation: land has no price-fraud rule
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא explains that שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף means something worth any amount of money, which is something with no אונאה rule. That describes land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: the phrase means 'something worth any money.' What is that? Something that has no price-fraud rule.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא answers the question from the last step. He reads שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף as 'worth any amount of money,' which fits land, since land has no אונאה rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With movable items, if the price was far off, the sale can be undone because of אונאה. With land, the sale stands no matter what price was paid, so land is 'worth whatever money' it was sold for. That is why the phrase points to land.

keyTerms.meaning: Price fraud. The rule that a sale at a price far from the real value can be fixed or cancelled.
Any amount of money
What is that? Which thing is meant?

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla says:
Something that is worth any amount of money.
What is that?
Something that has no price-fraud rule.
phrases.notes: That's land. A sale of land stands even if the price was way off.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא: דָּבָר הַשָּׁוֶה כֹּל כֶּסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 about how שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף means land.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the phrase שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף points to land.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means something worth any money, meaning something with no אונאה rule, which is land.

steps.title: Slaves and documents also have no price-fraud rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה בר עולא: עבדים and שטרות also have no אונאה rule, yet damages are not collected from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But slaves and documents also have no price-fraud rule!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first explanation. If 'no אונאה rule' is what the phrase means, then slaves and documents should count too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבדים and שטרות share land's feature of having no אונאה rule. But the ברייתא says בית דין collects only from land. So 'no אונאה rule' cannot be the feature the phrase is pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaves (here, Canaanite slaves)
Documents, such as loan documents
Also

phrases.english: Slaves and documents also
have no price-fraud rule!
phrases.notes: Yet the ברייתא only lets בית דין collect from land, not from these.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲבָדִים וּשְׁטָרוֹת נָמֵי אֵין לָהֶן אוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר עולא's explanation that the phrase means 'something with no אונאה rule'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The feature is too broad. It also covers עבדים and שטרות, which are not collected from.

steps.title: Second explanation: land is acquired with money
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא tries again: the phrase means something acquired by paying money, which is true of land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה בר עולא said: it means something that is acquired with money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא drops his first idea and offers a new one. Land can be acquired by paying money, and that is what the phrase is pointing to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Movable items are acquired by pulling or lifting them, not by paying money. Land can be acquired just by paying for it. So 'acquired with money' seems to separate land from movables.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Signals dropping the earlier answer for a new one.
Acquired by paying money
Acquiring something by handing over money

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba bar Ulla said:
Something that is acquired with money.
phrases.notes: Land can be bought just by paying. Movables need to be pulled or lifted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא: דָּבָר הַנִּקְנֶה בְּכֶסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation knocked down in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the phrase שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף points to land.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means something acquired with money, which is land.

steps.title: Slaves and documents are also acquired with money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second explanation: עבדים and שטרות can also be acquired with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: But slaves and documents are also acquired with money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second explanation the same way it knocked down the first. Slaves and documents also share this feature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again, the feature that was supposed to single out land also fits עבדים and שטרות. Since damages are not collected from those, 'acquired with money' cannot be what the phrase means either.

keyTerms.meaning: Are acquired

phrases.english: Slaves and documents also
are acquired with money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 11, in the same style as step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר עולא's second explanation, 'something acquired with money'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The feature is too broad. It also covers עבדים and שטרות.

steps.title: רב אשי: worth money, but not money itself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף means something worth money that is not money itself. Movables, slaves and documents all count as money, so only land is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: 'worth money' means it is not money itself, and all these other things count as money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the answer that works. The phrase says 'worth money,' not 'money,' so it means something that is not like money. All those other items are like money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי reads the words very closely: 'worth money' means something different from money. Movable items, slaves and documents are treated like money itself. That leaves land as the thing that is only 'worth money,' so the slaves-and-documents problem disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: And not money itself
All of these
They are

steps.whatToRemember: After two failed tries, רב אשי settles it: שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף means land, because everything else (movables, slaves, documents) counts as money itself.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
"Worth money" means not money itself,
and all of these are money.
phrases.notes: 'These' means movables, slaves and documents. They count as money itself, so only land is left.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף וְלֹא כֶּסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new explanation that avoids the problem raised in steps 10 and 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the phrase שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף points to land.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Worth money' excludes things that count as money itself. Movables, slaves and documents count as money, so the phrase means land.

steps.title: Contradiction: another ברייתא allows payment with anything, even bran
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר חיננא points out a contradiction. One ברייתא says בית דין collects only from land, while another says the word יָשִׁיב allows payment with any item worth money, even bran.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר חיננא raised a contradiction to רב הונא son of רב יהושע. One ברייתא teaches that 'worth money' means בית דין collects only from land. But another ברייתא teaches that 'he shall pay back' includes anything worth money, even bran!
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב יהודה בר חיננא sets two ברייתות side by side that seem to disagree about what a damager may pay with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא (from step 7) limits collection to land. The second ברייתא learns from the word יָשִׁיב that any item worth money is good for payment, even cheap bran. These seem to clash, and the גמרא now needs to resolve it.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction to him
Attend to, deal with
Property that serves as a guarantee, meaning land
He shall pay back
To include
Bran, a cheap leftover from grain

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against רב אשי. The גמרא accepts the reading of שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף and now asks how that ברייתא fits with a different ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר חִינָּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Ḥinnana raised a contradiction
to Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua:
It is taught: "Worth money"
teaches that the court does not attend
except to property that serves as a guarantee.
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא from step 7. 'Property that serves as a guarantee' means land.

phrases.english: But it is taught: "He shall pay back"
to include anything worth money,
and even bran!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר חִינָּנָא לְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 7 and sets it against another ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that says בית דין collects damages only from land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא learns from יָשִׁיב that any item worth money, even bran, is valid payment. That seems to contradict the land-only rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer to this contradiction will show how the land-only rule and the 'anything, even bran' rule can both be true.

steps.title: The land-only ברייתא is about collecting from orphans
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction from step 14. The ברייתא that says בית דין collects only from land is talking about collecting from יתומים whose father owed the damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? With orphans.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between the two ברייתות. The land-only rule applies when the person who owed the damages has died and we are collecting from his children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the payer can pay with anything worth money, even bran, as the second ברייתא says. But when the debtor has died, only the land his children inherited is tied to his debt. Inherited movables are not. So the two ברייתות describe different cases, and they no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: "What case are we dealing with here?" — a formula that limits a source to a specific situation in order to solve a problem
Orphans; here, the heirs of someone who owed money
A lien; property being legally tied to a debt

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule of debt collection that comes up across ש״ס: heirs pay their father's debts from inherited land, not from inherited movables.

phrases.english: With what case are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: "Here" means the ברייתא from step 14 that says בית דין collects only from land.

phrases.english: With orphans.
phrases.notes: He means the one who owed the damages died, and we are collecting from his children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 14 by placing the land-only ברייתא in a narrower case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting one source to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות talk about the same ordinary case, so they truly contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The land-only ברייתא deals with collecting from יתומים, where only inherited land is tied to the debt. The other ברייתא deals with the living damager himself, who may pay with anything worth money.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא lets the injured person collect from movables he grabbed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the orphans answer. The last part of that same ברייתא says that if the injured person grabbed movables first, בית דין collects for him from them. But orphans' inherited movables are not tied to the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the ברייתא is about orphans, look at its last part: if the injured person went ahead and grabbed movables, בית דין collects for him from them. If it's about orphans, why would בית דין collect for him from those movables?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 15 using the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said we are collecting from יתומים, whose inherited movables are not tied to the father's debt. Yet the end of the ברייתא lets the injured person keep and collect from movables he grabbed. If movables of orphans are not tied to the debt, grabbing them should not help him.

keyTerms.meaning: "Say the last part" — look at the end of the same source to test an explanation
He went ahead and grabbed (seized property on his own)
Movable property
The injured party

phrases.english: If it is about orphans, say the last part:
If the injured party went ahead and grabbed movables,
the court collects for him from them.
If it is about orphans, why
does the court collect for him from them?
phrases.notes: The problem is that an orphan's inherited movables aren't tied to his father's debt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the orphans answer of step 15 from the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the land-only ברייתא deals with יתומים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Movables of orphans are not tied to the father's debt. So the ברייתא's ruling that grabbed movables can be collected from does not fit a case about orphans.

steps.title: He grabbed the movables while the father was still alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with the rule of רבא in the name of רב נחמן: the injured person grabbed the movables while the damager was still alive, so he may keep them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: this is when he grabbed while the debtor was alive. Here too, he grabbed while the damager was alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 16. The grabbing in the end of the ברייתא happened before the father died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the father died, his movables passed to the orphans free of his debt. But if the injured person already took hold of them while the father was alive, they were never part of what the orphans inherited. So the ברייתא can still be about orphans, and the injured person keeps what he grabbed.

keyTerms.meaning: While (the debtor) was alive
Here too — applying an existing rule to the current case

steps.whatToRemember: The land-only ברייתא is about orphans. Their inherited land pays the father's debts, but their inherited movables do not, unless the injured person grabbed them while the father was still alive.

phrases.english: As Rava said that Rav Naḥman said:
That he seized while (the debtor was) alive;
here too, it is where he seized while (the damager was) alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16, so the orphans answer of step 15 stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case by applying an established rule from another source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The grabbing happened after the father's death, when the movables already belonged to the orphans free of the debt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The grabbing happened during the father's lifetime, so the injured person keeps the movables even though the ברייתא is about orphans.

steps.title: Quoting the next phrase of the משנה: before a court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on and quotes the next words of the משנה, ״בפני בית דין״, in order to explain them.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Before a court" —
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is quoting the next phrase of the משנה so that it can explain it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of שוה כסף and collecting from land is finished. The גמרא now goes back to the משנה's list of terms and picks up the next one. The explanation itself comes right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: Before a court — the next phrase of the משנה about the conditions for paying damages

phrases.english: "Before a court" —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the שוה כסף discussion and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the משנה's phrase ״בפני בית דין״ for explanation in the next step.

steps.title: First explanation: leaving out someone who sold his land before court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's first explanation of ״בפני בית דין״ is that בית דין only collects from land the damager still owns when he comes to court. If he sold his land before that, they do not collect from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words ״בפני בית דין״ come to leave out a person who sells his property and only afterward goes to court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first explanation of the words ״בפני בית דין״ that it quoted in step 18. It reads them as limiting which land בית דין may collect from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that בית דין collects damages from land. This explanation adds a limit: the land must still belong to the damager when the case comes ״before the court.″ Land he sold before the court case would be off limits.

keyTerms.meaning: This comes to exclude / leave out
One who sells his property (here, his land)
And afterward

phrases.english: This excludes one who sells his property
and afterward goes to court.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּרָט לְמוֹכֵר נְכָסָיו וְאַחַר כָּךְ הוֹלֵךְ לְבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the implied question of step 18: what do the words ״בפני בית דין״ come to teach?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the words ״בפני בית דין״ add?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They leave out land that the damager sold before he came to court.

steps.title: Challenge: then a lender couldn't collect from land sold after the loan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the first explanation. If that were true, then a borrower who sold his land before the court case would also escape payment, and that cannot be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we really learn from this that if someone borrowed money, then sold his land, and only afterward came to court, בית דין does not collect the debt for the lender from that land?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from step 19. It shows that the explanation leads to a conclusion that cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is a known rule that a loan makes the borrower's land answer for the debt from the time of the loan, even if he sells it later. If ״בפני בית דין״ meant that land sold before court is off limits, the same logic would wrongly protect a borrower who sold his land. So the explanation in step 19 cannot stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (here said with surprise: should we really learn this?!)
He borrowed
They collect payment

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the lender truly can't collect. The ?! shows this is a wrong conclusion that the גמרא uses to knock down the explanation in step 19.

phrases.english: Should we learn from this
that one who borrowed and then sold his property,
and afterward came to court,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּית דִּין גּוֹבִין לוֹ מֵהֶן?!
phrases.english: the court does not collect for him from them?!
phrases.notes: "Him" is the lender, and "them" is the land the borrower already sold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation offered in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that ״בפני בית דין״ leaves out land sold before the court case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio: by the same logic a lender could not collect from land sold after the loan. That contradicts the accepted rule that a debt takes hold of the land from the time of the loan.

steps.title: New explanation: leaving out a court of non-ordained judges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the first explanation. It explains instead that ״בפני בית דין״ means a real, qualified court, which leaves out a court of הדיוטות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the words ״בפני בית דין״ come to leave out a court of הדיוטות, judges who do not have סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation of ״בפני בית דין״ to replace the one rejected in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are no longer about which land can be collected from. They are now about who the judges must be. Only a properly qualified court can rule on these damages, so a court of הדיוטות is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier idea and gives a new one)
Ordinary people; here, judges without סמיכה
A court made up of judges who did not receive סמיכה

steps.whatToRemember: ״בפני בית דין״ is not a limit on which land can be collected from. It teaches that the case must come before a qualified court, not a court of הדיוטות.

phrases.english: Rather, it excludes a court of non-ordained judges.
phrases.notes: Literally "a court of commoners," meaning judges who never received סמיכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation of step 19 after the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״בפני בית דין״ limits collection to land the damager still owns when he comes to court.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״בפני בית דין״ requires a qualified court and leaves out a court of הדיוטות.

steps.title: Quoting the next words of the משנה: "Based on witnesses"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on and quotes the next words of the משנה, ״על פי עדים״, so it can explain them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: ״על פי עדים״, based on witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה and is getting ready to explain them in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that ״בפני בית דין״ has been explained, the גמרא keeps going in order through the משנה's words. The explanation of ״על פי עדים״ comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Based on / by the word of
Witnesses
The משנה's phrase: payment is made based on the testimony of witnesses

phrases.english: "Based on witnesses" —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from ״בפני בית דין״ to the next words of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה teaches that payment is made based on the testimony of witnesses. The explanation follows in the next step.

steps.title: Witnesses exclude someone who already admitted to a fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that ״על פי עדים״ excludes a person who admitted to a קנס and only afterward had witnesses testify. He is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words 'by witnesses' come to exclude someone who admits he owes a fine, and only later do witnesses come. He is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the words ״על פי עדים״ that it quoted in the last step. They teach that payment must come through witnesses, so a person who admitted first is פטור even if witnesses show up later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a person who admits he owes a קנס does not have to pay it. The גמרא reads ״על פי עדים״ as teaching that this exemption still holds after witnesses arrive. Once he has admitted, later testimony does not make him pay.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; this comes to leave out a certain case
One who admits on his own that he owes a fine
A fine, a payment set by the תורה that is not just covering the actual loss
Exempt; does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: ״על פי עדים״ here does not simply mean 'you need witnesses to prove the case.' The גמרא is reading it to exclude one specific case: someone who admitted first, before the witnesses came.

phrases.english: To exclude one who admits to a fine
and afterward witnesses came,
that he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּרָט לְמוֹדֶה בִּקְנָס וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what the quoted words ״על פי עדים״ come to teach.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״על פי עדים״ excludes someone who admitted to a קנס before witnesses came. He remains פטור.

steps.title: This explanation only works for one opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation. It works for the view that such a person is פטור, but there is also a view that he is חייב. For that view, what do the words ״על פי עדים״ teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says that a person who admits to a fine, and afterward witnesses come, is exempt. But for the one who says he is liable, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from step 23. It shows that the explanation only works according to one side of a known disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that once a person admits to a קנס, later witnesses cannot make him pay. Others hold that the witnesses do make him חייב. According to the second view, the explanation from step 23 is false, so the גמרא asks why the משנה would say ״על פי עדים״ for that view.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well; it fits
According to the one who says
Liable; has to pay
What is there to say? A formula meaning that this view has no explanation yet

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says:
one who admits to a fine
and afterward witnesses came is exempt.
But according to the one who says:
one who admits to a fine
and afterward witnesses came is liable,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation in step 23 by showing it does not fit every opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that ״על פי עדים״ excludes someone who admitted to a קנס before witnesses came
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that later witnesses make him חייב, there is nothing for these words to exclude. The phrase would then teach nothing for that view.

steps.title: The phrase is needed to set up the next clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: ״על פי עדים״ is not there to exclude a case. It is needed to lead into the סיפא, the next part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for the latter clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the challenge, and the answer continues past this line. It says the משנה wrote ״על פי עדים״ to set up its next words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer changes what the phrase is for. It does not need to exclude any case. It simply introduces the סיפא, which describes which witnesses are accepted. This way the phrase makes sense even for the view that a person who admits is חייב once witnesses come.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause; the later part of a משנה
It was needed for it; the wording was necessary for that purpose

phrases.english: It is needed for the latter clause
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going after this. The סיפא is the next part of the משנה, about which kinds of people count as witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24 by giving the phrase a purpose that fits every opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the phrase a new job: it introduces the next clause instead of excluding a case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״על פי עדים״ must be excluding some case, and that only works for the view that admission exempts him.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״על פי עדים״ is needed as an introduction to the סיפא about which witnesses qualify, so it is necessary for every opinion.
